headlines.title: Man rescued from inside garbage truck in San Francisco
headlines.description: A man was rescued from inside a garbage truck early Wednesday morning in San Francisco, according to the fire department. Firefighters were dispatched around 4:11 a.m. to the 100 block of Mason Street following a report of a person trapped inside a Recology garbage truck. According to SFFD, the truck’s driver had been flagged down and told that someone could be heard yelling from inside the garbage area of the truck. About 25 firefighters responded to the scene, and the rescue operation took roughly two hours, according to fire officials. The man was eventually rescued and was conscious, breathing and talking before being taken to a hospital, according to a San Francisco Fire Department spokesperson. The extent of his injuries was not immediately known. A firefighter also suffered a laceration to the hand during the rescue and was taken to a hospital for stitches, fire officials added. A fire official said he is believed to have entered a dumpster looking for food before he got trapped in the garbage truck. Bay City News contributed to this report
headlines.source: Joel Soria and Ginger Conejero Saab

headlines.title: AI boom heats up Bay Area housing market as wealthy buyers drive demand for high-end homes across U.S.
headlines.description: Here’s another place the AI frenzy is making itself felt: the market for luxury homes. High-income earners, many of them employees at AI companies, are snapping up multimillion-dollar houses in the San Francisco Bay Area, undaunted by the higher mortgage rates and rising home prices that have prevented many would-be buyers from affording a home. The Bay Area buying spree is the clearest manifestation of a nationwide trend of sales of upper-end properties largely holding up better than sales of less expensive homes. Metro areas such as San Diego, Miami, Detroit, Nashville and Tampa, Florida, are also seeing upper-market homes sell at a faster pace. The hotter market for luxury properties comes at a time when the broader housing market remains stuck in a yearslong rut. Sales of previously occupied U.S. homes were essentially flat last year, moored at a 30-year low. Most recently, they slowed again in July. Sales of newly built homes, which make up a far smaller part of the housing market, are also down this year. Underpinning the luxury market are affluent home shoppers who can afford to shrug off rising mortgage rates and often pay all cash for a home or come up with a large down payment by raising funds through sales of stocks or other investments. Stock market gains powered by the artificial intelligence boom have helped boost investors’ portfolios. The benchmark S&P 500 is up solidly this year and remains near its most recent all-time high. “These people have lots of money and they’re just not going to be very sensitive to things like mortgage rates or home prices,” said Daryl Fairweather, chief economist at Redfin. “They want the home they want and they have the money to buy it.” The trend is the housing market version of the “K-shaped” economy, where wealthier households pull ahead of middle- and lower-income ones. In this case, many would-be homebuyers remain on the sideline while affluent buyers drive sales of luxury homes. Sales of pricier homes are holding up better Nationally, sales of luxury homes, defined as properties in the top 5% of a metro area by price, rose 2% in the first half of this year, compared to the same period in 2025, according to data from Redfin. Sales of middle-of-the-market homes, or properties closest to an area’s median price, rose 1.9% in the same period. The dichotomy in the market can better be seen in price appreciation. The median sales price of a luxury home nationally between January and June was roughly $1.37 million, a 4.3% increase from a year earlier. For homes in the middle of the market, the median sales price rose 1.4% to $377,245. In the San Francisco metro area, sales of luxury homes soared 39.3% in the first half of this year compared to a year earlier, while middle-market home sales surged 15.1%. And across the bay in Oakland, sales of upper-market homes jumped 13.3%, while sales of middle-market properties rose 3.9%. Several other metro areas not plugged into the AI boom are also seeing sales and price growth for luxury homes. Among the most notable examples: in the Tampa metro area, luxury home sales surged 35.5% in the January-June period, while sales of middle-market homes fell 5.1%. In Nashville, sales of upper-market homes jumped 10.8%, while sales of middle-market properties rose only 1.7%. And in Detroit, sales of higher-end properties vaulted 8.7% compared to a 6% decline in sales of middle-market homes. All told, sales of luxury homes so far this year are outpacing or have declined less than those of middle-market homes in 44% of the nation’s 50 largest metro areas. Urgency to buy a home before potential AI IPOs In the Bay Area, tech companies bent on winning the race to develop artificial intelligence into a profitable business have juiced compensation to recruit talented executives and software engineers, widening the pool of high-income earners. Many of these employees have been buying homes, often outdoing rival buyers by offering well above the asking price, real estate agents say. The Bay Area housing market could get even hotter should two of the biggest names in AI follow through on their intent to become publicly traded companies. OpenAI, creator of ChatGPT, and Anthropic, home to Claude, filed preliminary paperwork in June for initial public offerings. Neither has yet decided on the timing. An analysis by Redfin that looked at how much employees at both companies stand to gain potentially from the companies going public estimated that the combined IPO earnings would be enough to buy nearly one-third of all homes in San Francisco. Just the possibility of these two blockbuster IPOs is building pressure on some home shoppers in the Bay Area to buy sooner, rather than later. They worry they’ll face a flood of newly minted millionaires ready to pounce, further ratcheting up competition in the San Francisco housing market. Julio Bermudez, an AI data infrastructure company executive in the Bay Area, had been looking to buy his first home for about a year, but his search took on new urgency. “So, you start taking a look at that and you take a look at your own position — both from just a diversification standpoint, as well as the fact that we’re trying to set roots here, kids are in school, all that good stuff,” said Bermudez, 41. ”And it’s like we don’t want to be priced out, so we need to buy now.” Recently, Bermudez entered into a contract to buy a five-bedroom, four-bath house in Orinda, about 17 miles northeast of San Francisco. The seller was asking $3.5 million, but agreed to sell for $3.3 million. “I felt like this was sort of an interesting time and location to try to strike before it really does get crazy,” he said.

headlines.title: SF high school's varsity baseball coaching staff removed after racial incident
headlines.description: A San Francisco high school has lost its entire varsity baseball coaching staff and must forfeit some games following a racial incident. The San Francisco Unified School District did not elaborate on what happened, but the San Francisco Chronicle reported it involved alleged race-based taunting by Lowell High School varsity players during a game in May against Lincoln High School. Following an investigation by the school district, the varsity coaching staff at Lowell has been removed and the school will forfeit regular season games against three schools, including Lincoln. In a statement, the district said, “…there is no place for racism, discrimination, or racialized harm in the Lowell community or anywhere in SFUSD.” Parents said it’s difficult to know if the district made the right call because it didn’t release enough details about the incident.

headlines.title: Police round up dozens of abandoned vehicles in East Oakland
headlines.description: Police in Oakland rounded up dozens of abandoned vehicles following feedback the department got in August during National Night Out, the department said Tuesday. Officers received complaints about urban blight and launched a sweep of East Oakland, collecting 60 abandoned and stolen vehicles, police said. Beginning Monday, tow operations were carried out in the 300 and 1400 blocks of 105th Avenue, the 1300 block of 104th Avenue, the 1300 block of 102nd Avenue and the 600 block of Hegenberger Road. Police said the vehicles were linked to violent crime, narcotics activity and the dismantling of unregistered cars left on public streets. In total, 41 abandoned vehicles were towed, two stolen vehicles were recovered, and more than 20 additional vehicles were tagged for towing, the department said. “Several residents shared that, for the first time in months, they were able to park in front of their homes after the vehicles were removed,” OPD said. To report abandoned vehicles in Oakland, email vehicleabatement@oaklandca.gov. or call 510-777-8538.

headlines.title: Aisha Wahab sworn into Congress to fill Eric Swalwell's seat
headlines.description: California Sen. Aisha Wahab was officially sworn into the U.S. House of Representatives on Wednesday, becoming the first Afghan American to serve in Congress. Wahab is filling the state’s 14th Congressional District seat, vacated by former Rep. Eric Swalwell, who resigned from Congress in April after being accused of sexual assault and harassment. He has denied the allegations. Wahab will face BART Board President Melissa Hernandez in the November general election to determine who will serve the next full two-year term. Early voting and vote-by-mail begin Oct. 5. Election Day is Nov. 3.

headlines.title: Driver arrested on suspicion of DUI, manslaughter after passenger dies in San Bruno crash
headlines.description: The driver of a car that hit a pole in San Bruno last weekend, killing a passenger, has been arrested on suspicion of driving under the influence and manslaughter, police said Tuesday. Early Sunday morning just before 1 a.m., officers responded to a solo vehicle crash near the intersection of El Camino Real and the westbound Interstate 380 off-ramp, according to police. The vehicle hit a light pole. The driver, a 29-year-old San Francisco man and his passenger, a 22-year-old San Francisco man, both sustained major injuries and the passenger later died. Investigators allege that the driver was operating the car while under the influence of alcohol or drugs, police said. The driver was arrested on suspicion of DUI and booked into jail on suspicion of gross vehicular manslaughter, DUI causing bodily injury or death and being in possession of a controlled substance. Police are not releasing the name of the driver or of the deceased passenger.

headlines.title: San Jose officials to vote on new name for downtown plaza
headlines.description: San Jose is one step closer to choosing a new name for its downtown plaza, with the options now narrowed to two. The plaza was previously named for labor leader Cesar Chavez, but city workers covered his name following serious allegations of sexual assault and misconduct against Chavez. The city then opened the renaming process to the public, with about 10,000 San Jose residents weighing in. As part of the process, the city sought a name that would honor the people behind the farmworker labor movement rather than one individual. Of the dozens of suggestions submitted, two finalists will go before the San Jose Parks and Recreation Commission for a vote Wednesday: Plaza de San Jose, which received the most public support, and Farmworker Plaza. The commission is scheduled to meet at 5:30 p.m. at the Roosevelt Community Center near East Santa Clara and 20th streets. People who cannot attend in person can watch the meeting online. The name selected by the commission will be recommended to the full San Jose City Council, which is expected to make a final decision in October. San Jose Aug 25 San Jose Jun 24 San Jose Aug 2 Last day to weigh in on new name for San Jose's downtown plaza

headlines.title: Proposed church purchase of historic Antioch theater sparks community concern
headlines.description: A historic East Bay venue that has hosted performances and community events for nearly a century could soon have a new owner, raising concerns among residents about the theater’s future. The El Campanil Theatre in Antioch’s Rivertown district is currently in escrow to be purchased by a local church, with the sale potentially closing as early as October. Community members gathered at the venue for a public meeting to discuss the impending transition and raise awareness about the sale. “I think we need to start mobilizing people to let them know this place is being sold,” one community member said during the meeting. “I don’t think everybody knows that.” The property fell into financial struggles during the COVID-19 pandemic and was sold to an out-of-state owner. It went back on the market nine months ago. Last month, Legendary Movement Church raised the down payment necessary to acquire the building. For residents and preservationists, the sale threatens the last remaining venue of its kind in the area. “This is the last remaining theatre in our city that’s being operated as a theatre,” said Sharon Sobel Idul, president of the El Campanil Theatre Preservation Foundation. Local residents expressed heartbreak over the potential loss of community programming and shared personal connections to the landmark. “There’s no other place to have music revues, plays, this is the last one left,” said Antioch resident Lisa Schmidt. “We grew up here…first dates here…we did recitals here,” added Antioch resident Michelle Fanucchi. Eli Herrera, lead pastor of Legendary Movement Church, attended the community meeting to hear residents’ concerns directly. He emphasized that the church aims to support the local area, though church services and events will take priority once the deal is complete. “This is the message I’ve given our church. We’re not a church in the city, we’re a church for the city,” Herrera said. Herrera noted that while the church wants to work with the community, external events will need to adapt to the new owner’s calendar. “Like any owner that takes over a building…when you go in its your house, we’re not fitting into the schedule they have because otherwise they would be purchasing the building,” Herrera said. The property remains in escrow, and the current owner hopes to finalize the sale by October.

headlines.title: Did we find dark matter? Here's how a Bay Area lab is helping with the possible breakthrough
headlines.description: Dark matter is legendary. It’s given credit for possibly explaining how the universe works, but we’ve never been able to actually identify it, until now – maybe. On Tuesday, excitement was high in the science community, especially in the Bay Area, due to a possible dark matter discovery. Among the researchers spending decades searching for dark matter are those working at the SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory in Menlo Park. They say it’s early – after all, they’re looking for something that’s invisible – but if what they found truly is dark matter, it could open up a lot of new science.

headlines.title: Demolition company donates hundreds of items from razed Millbrae inn
headlines.description: A South Bay company that tore down the historic El Rancho Inn in Millbrae gave away hundreds of beds and other furnishings from inside the rooms to those in need. Buccaneer Demolition in San Jose was hired to tear down the Inn, which was built in 1948 and featured in the movie “The Right Stuff,” to make way for more than 350 new housing units. The company decided not to destroy the furniture inside but instead set it aside to give away. Buccaneer Demolition Vice President Jose Uribe said they donated roughly 487 items, including mattresses, microwaves, coffeemakers, chairs and more. “It’s important to us as an organization to do our best to limit the debris in the landfill and try to reuse items that still have life, that serve purpose,” Uribe said. “There’s a lot of value in a lot of the items that we salvage.” Most of the furnishings were donated to Farmworker Caravan, which supports agriculture workers from Gilroy to Half Moon Bay. Executive Director Darlene Tenes said for some clients the mattresses and bed frames were a game changer. “Sometimes when they get a bed, it’s the first bed they’ve ever slept in,” Tenes said. “They’ve never had a bed before. It’s such a huge, big gift.” Furnishings from some of the demolished rooms were also donated to Bay Area Furniture Bank, which supports the unhoused population, domestic violence victims and low-income families. Buccaneer Demolition also donated a statue from the inn to a Millbrae historical museum.

headlines.title: Colorado Fire: Wildfire near Yosemite burns 250 acres, prompts evacuations
headlines.description: Firefighters are responding to a wildfire burning near Yosemite National Park in Mariposa County. The Colorado Fire, which started Tuesday near Highway 140 and Colorado Road, has burned 250 acres in the Midpines area and remains at zero percent containment, according to Cal Fire. The cause of the blaze remains under investigation. As of Tuesday afternoon, the fire was moving at a moderate rate of spread toward the Merced River drainage. A total of 126 personnel from the Cal Fire Madera-Mariposa-Merced Unit are deployed to the incident, supported by 14 fire engines, four helicopters, three water tenders, two bulldozers, and three hand crews. Numerous air tankers from across the state are also making fire suppression runs as weather conditions allow. Crews are attempting to construct control lines to hold the flames north of Colorado Road, east of Telegraph Road, west of Buffalo Road, and south of the Merced River. Colorado Fire prompts evacuation orders in Mariposa County Emergency officials have issued mandatory evacuation orders and warnings for several zones in Mariposa County due to the immediate and potential threats to life and property: Evacuation Orders: Issued for zones Mariposa 546, 548, and 549. Residents in these areas are lawfully ordered to leave immediately. Evacuation Warnings: Issued for zone Mariposa 550 and 551. Those who require extra time to evacuate or have pets and livestock are advised to leave now. An evacuation shelter for residents and small animals has been established at New Life Christian Church, located at 5089 Cole Road in Mariposa. County officials have set up accommodation for large animals at multiple facilities and can be reached for arrangements at 209-967-3615. Road closures in effect due to Colorado Fire near Yosemite Road closures remain in effect, including state Route 140 from Briceburg to the Bug Hostel. Cal Fire reports that 45 structures are threatened by the fire, down slightly from earlier estimates. No injuries or destroyed structures have been reported. Yosemite still open while crews battle Colorado Fire Yosemite National Park remains open and is not currently threatened. “Crews will continue their fire fight throughout the night to control the fire and mitigate further damage,” Cal Fire said in a statement Tuesday night.

headlines.title: New video shows Eric Swalwell's stop by federal agents at SFO
headlines.description: Newly released surveillance video shows former East Bay Congressman Eric Swalwell being approached and escorted through San Francisco International Airport by federal agents. The footage was released by airport authorities in response to a public records request by NBC Bay Area’s Investigative Unit. The video appears to show federal agents approaching and surrounding Swalwell near the gate shortly after his arrival to San Francisco’s International Airport on Aug. 15. Swalwell, who is seen wearing a black hoodie sweater and baseball hat, appears to cooperate as he hands what looks like his cellphone to a female agent. He is seen carrying a backpack and rolling suitcase as the agents escort him through the airport, up an escalator and into a restricted area. Court records show federal agents executed a search warrant at SFO at approximately 8:25 p.m. The property inventory identifies the seized items as a white Apple iPhone, a charging cable and adapter, and an Apple MacBook Pro. The following day, federal agents searched Swalwell’s Washington, D.C., residence. He has not been charged with a crime. California Aug 20 Congress Apr 13 Publicly available warrant records cite a federal civil rights statute, Title 18, Section 242, which makes it a crime for someone acting under government authority to willfully deprive another person of federally protected rights. Multiple women have accused the former congressman of misconduct, including sexual assault and sending unsolicited explicit messages. Swalwell has denied the allegations, describing them through his attorney as false and politically motivated. Swalwell resigned from Congress and ended his campaign for California governor in April after the allegations became public. Before his resignation, the House Ethics Committee had announced its own investigation, while emphasizing that opening an inquiry did not mean a violation had occurred. The FBI previously declined to comment on the circumstances surrounding the airport encounter. Swalwell and his attorneys have not addressed the incident.
